findings.correction: run_fact_check() (tools/aris_homepage.py ~L1373-1493) checks bibkey existence, DBLP title hit/no-hit/ambiguity, year mismatch, venue mismatch (fuzzy), and award-badge-needs-a-verifiable-URL sanity — it never checks author lists.

findings.claim: Paper action links can come from publications.bib url/eprint fields, in addition to profile.yml's publications_meta.<bibkey>.links
findings.correction: build_publications_section() (tools/aris_homepage.py ~L904-986) reads links EXCLUSIVELY from profile.yml's publications_meta.<bibkey>.links. A url/eprint field in publications.bib is valid BibTeX but is never read for rendering link buttons.

rounds.confirmed_claims_summary: Script filename/underscore, no installed aris-homepage alias, pyyaml requirement, pdftotext subprocess call + poppler-utils error message, render/check auto-audit with PASS/WARN/BLOCKED semantics (WARN non-blocking, BLOCKED blocks unless --override-all), fact-check never writing links/thumbnails back to files, identity.photo base64/URL embed with no fetching, the init→extraction.json→finalize→render pipeline and finalize's clear die() on missing extraction.json, theory-minimal valid / active-researcher hard-disabled, and that the Windows-environment claims (.py file-association silence, python3 App Execution Alias stub, pdftotext non-ASCII path mangling, urllib.request-based SSL/pip-system-certs fix) are correctly attributed as external OS/tool behavior rather than script behavior — all CONFIRMED against source.

rounds.notes: Targeted fixes for the two WRONG findings above were correct, but a lingering sentence (near the end of the '主仓库 README 演示图...' section) still told users to add missing links/thumbnails in both profile.yml AND publications.bib. maintainer_review.why: The contributor's own gpt-5.4 audit was real work and caught two genuine overclaims, but it did not re-derive the audit verdict semantics or the Windows dependency chain. A maintainer pass against tools/aris_homepage.py found further errors and moved the files out of docs/.
corrections_landed: A fact-check hard failure yields verdict BLOCKED and `render` exits WITHOUT writing index.html — the guide had said the result only affects marks in the audit report (aris_homepage.py:1364-1371, :682).
`.docx` was recommended as the no-pdftotext fallback; on Windows it needs `python-docx` (textutil is macOS-only). `.txt` is the only zero-install format (:496-506).
Both conda examples were unrunnable: `render` treats cwd as the workspace, so from the site dir the script path must be `..\tools\aris_homepage.py` (:671).
The English edition billed itself as a tested sequence but never installed `pyyaml` and opened with a `.pdf` needing poppler (:619, :512).
The error table quoted pdftotext's `I/O Error`, which `capture_output=True, check=True` swallows — the user sees an uncaught CalledProcessError instead (:509, :340).
Python 3.10+ (the floor declared in SKILL.md) was not stated; the guide accepted any version.
Fact-check scope corrected: DBLP only (ARXIV_API is defined but never called), only `selected_publications` entries, no author check, award sanity accepts only 5 link fields.
The two editions are now faithful siblings; each previously carried facts the other omitted.
maintainer_review.relocated: docs/ is published verbatim by pages.yml with no Jekyll, so a .md there ships as raw markdown, docs/aris-homepage-windows/ would 404, and ../skills ../tools links would break on the site. The guides now sit beside the skill they document and are linked from README, README_CN and SKILL.md.
not_done_deliberately: No hashes re-stamped: the original `source_sha256` fields were dropped rather than refreshed. Nothing consumes them outside docs/, and tools/verify_reviews.py only walks docs/**/*.html.
No render pipeline entry, manifest row, CI check or test was added for these two files — they are read on GitHub, next to SKILL.md, like PROFILE_SCHEMA.md.
Reviewer proposals declined as out-of-scope for a first-run Windows guide: expired-per-paper-override BLOCKED path, and the nuance that PASS can occur with zero selected papers.
